assets.titleEn: Luna discovers the photograph · live-action video
assets.prompt: ONE continuous 5-second LIVE-ACTION photographic shot, starting from this exact image. Preserve this exact fictional Luna, her facial identity, low ponytail, plain charcoal T-shirt and olive cargos, the same attic, trunk, light and composition. She lifts the small old photograph just 4 centimetres closer to her face, with both hands still holding its edges. Her eyes trace the photo, she blinks once and her tense eyebrows relax into a very subtle quiet curiosity, almost recognition. Keep her mouth closed; no speech, no crying, no large smile. The photograph remains a rigid real piece of paper, its back turned toward camera; it must not bend, transform, reveal animated pictures or multiply. Her face remains clearly visible throughout. Camera makes an almost imperceptible 5-centimetre push-in; no cut, no sudden zoom, no reframing. Natural skin pores, real hair flyaways, cotton texture, practical window light, human microexpressions and believable finger anatomy. Keep the photorealistic live-action look; no painting, brushstrokes, CGI or beauty smoothing. Silent performance, no music, captions or lettering.

qa.notes: Inspected 15 evenly sampled frames: Luna's identity remains consistent, photograph lifts then stays rigid in both hands; restrained gaze and recognizable live-action face. No funeral props or text introduced. Full playback listening not performed.

assets.title: Flashback · transition continue expérimentale

At 1.8s the foreground heel presses into the wood; a brief realistic flare from the LEFT window momentarily washes the whole frame over about 4–6 frames. During this full-frame bright exposure, use a SINGLE HARD EDIT to the memory: same spatially aligned black high-top shoe now less worn, no cream repair, white tube sock with two burgundy stripes, rough asphalt Bronx court at warm sunset, matching final reference exactly. 2.2–5s the memory resolves and holds with subtle natural balance. This is an EDIT TRANSITION hidden by practical light, not physical transformation: no visible shoe morph, no dissolving flesh, no growth of socks, no portals or particles, no camera orbit, no rotation, no extra feet, no titles. Exactly two human feet, convincing materials, natural light, photographic grain, never painted or animated.

assets.title: Luna ajoute sa propre trace · vidéo réaliste
assets.titleFr: Luna ajoute sa propre trace · vidéo réaliste
assets.titleEn: Luna adds her own mark · live-action video
assets.prompt: ONE continuous 5-second LIVE-ACTION macro insert, starting from this exact photographic frame. Keep the same single old black high-top shoe firmly supported on Luna's olive cargo-clad knee; same cream laces, canvas fibres, frayed cream repair, aged rubber, hands, marker and warm attic light. A single precise action: her right hand slowly completes ONE short orange diagonal stroke, about 1.5 centimetres long, across the existing cream repair where the nib is already touching. The orange line appears only directly behind the moving nib. At 3 seconds she lifts the marker straight away by 3 centimetres, then holds still for the remaining 2 seconds so we can read this small new personal mark. Her left hand stabilizes the heel without changing grip. No second mark, no added text, no filling the whole patch, no other gesture. The mark never touches a logo. Keep the entire shoe geometry absolutely consistent, no melting, no floating, no duplicated fingers or changing laces. Fixed camera, no cuts, no rotation, focus stays on nib and repair. Genuine photographic skin and textile microtexture, practical soft light; no gouache, cartoon or 3D-render materials. No speech, music, subtitles or overlay.

qa.notes: Inspected 15 evenly sampled frames: one orange marking action then the marker lifts and holds, stable shoe and fingers. Orange becomes a broad short stroke across roughly the upper half of the cream repair rather than the requested fine 1.5cm line; no logo touched. Candidate with this visual deviation disclosed.

assets.titleEn: Luna starts her own path · live-action video
assets.prompt: ONE continuous 5-second LIVE-ACTION wide shot from this exact starting image. Preserve the exact existing fictional Luna, charcoal T-shirt, olive cargos, low ponytail, inherited worn black high-top shoes, plain black grip tape skateboard, brick courtyard and natural late-afternoon light. This is one gentle, controlled first skate push, no tricks: the foot already on the front half of the deck stays planted there throughout; the foot initially on the pavement pushes backward ONCE along the ground, then lifts and lands on the rear half of the same deck. The board rolls steadily forward toward screen right, only about two metres. She glides quietly for the final second with both feet on the board and relaxed bent knees. Four wheels remain below the deck and in contact with pavement; real wheel rotation, accurate weight transfer, plausible balance and anatomy. The top of the board remains plain black grip tape; never expose or invent printed artwork. Keep the same clothes, shoes, hair and body proportions. Camera makes a small smooth side-follow movement to retain her full body, both shoes and entire skateboard in frame at all times; no cut, no dramatic zoom or orbit. Photographic human skin, natural cloth and sunlight, subtle real motion blur, not animation or a game render. Quiet hope and self-confidence. No speech, captions, titles or music.

qa.notes: Inspected 15 evenly sampled frames: one grounded skate push followed by both feet on deck and gentle gliding, coherent limb motion, board stays below feet, full body and board remain visible. Plain dark grip retained. Fine wheel motion requires normal-speed team review.

assets.placement: Après le geste personnel et le départ du grenier, avant la signature.
assets.recommendation: Une seule poussée puis une glisse. Le détail orange est très peu visible à cette échelle ; éviter de raccorder ensuite sur une réparation vierge en gros plan.
